detail.body:
## Motivation

Depends on #31700 (merged).

DeepSeek-V4 two-batch overlap (TBO) with DP attention, `moe_a2a_backend=none` and attention TP > 1 applied full-TP variable-length collectives to tensors replicated within each attention-TP group. On older `main` this corrupted the gather and combine layouts and produced invalid output (the H100 report below); on current `main` the same configuration fails in the TBO gather, because each child's DP counts have one entry per TP rank (`dp_slot_in`: "a per-replica sequence of 4 entries does not belong to a DP gather of width 2").

This change gives each full-TP rank one shard of its replicated DP-local tensor and reconstructs the DP-local result across the attention-TP group after the combine, and fixes the problems the same configuration hit next.

## Modifications

Original commits:
- Derive and validate DP-local token counts and full-TP shard counts for each TBO child batch.
- Shard replicated hidden states and input IDs across attention-TP ranks before the full-TP variable-length gather.
- Reduce-scatter the MoE output into one shard per full-TP rank, then all-gather within the attention-TP group to reconstruct the replicated DP-local output.
- Select the non-EP TBO strategy for CP 1, multi-rank DP and SUM_LEN padding; MAX_LEN batches take the non-overlapped path.
- Exercise attention TP in the registered DeepSeek-V4 TBO tests (AMD and H200) and add focused tests for collective-size mapping and validation.

Added after review:
- **Empty micro-batch.** TBO can split a short extend so that one micro-batch has no tokens on any DP rank; the overlapped MoE then ran the experts on zero rows, and the triton runner's fused SiLU-and-mul with the SwiGLU clamp rejected the zero-block launch, crashing the server on a single short request (also on `main`). The experts are now skipped for such a micro-batch; every rank gathers the same rows, so all skip together.
- **Eager decode at attention TP > 1.** TBO children are padded to a multiple of attention TP tokens, but a decode child kept its request count, so a one-request child carried two token rows and DeepSeek-V4's decode metadata asserted (`req_pool_indices 1, out_cache_loc 2`). A decode child now pads its requests with its tokens, as `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` does for the whole batch.
- **Shared expert locality.** The TBO path again computes a replicated TP1 shared expert on local rows only under `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL`; inside the MoE it is added on TP rank 0 and the reducing combine counts it once (verified below).
- **AMD unit test stub.** `DeepseekV2MoE` now always sets `shared_experts`, and `forward_normal` reads it directly; the MoE stub in `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py` is built with `__new__` and failed with "no attribute 'shared_experts'" on MI35x. The stub now sets it to `None`.
- **AMD chat probe.** The single-request check added to the AMD TBO test runs on a server that thinks by default (`SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1`), so the reasoning counted against `max_tokens: 32` and the reply was cut off before the answer (`'7 + 5 equals'`). The budget is now 512 tokens, and a failure reports `finish_reason`.
- **ROCm.** The combine's attention-TP all-gather runs on the TBO communication stream while the other micro-batch's attention uses the same group's collectives on the compute stream. On ROCm `all_gather_into_tensor` takes aiter's custom all-gather, and MI355X failed later in unrelated kernels with "invalid configuration argument" (this PR's AMD CI failure), passing with `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AG=0`. The shards now go through the attention-TP device process group.

## Accuracy Tests

### H200, after review

8×H200, torch 2.14.1+cu130, sgl-kernel 0.4.10, FlashInfer 0.7.2.

- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, 5-shot GSM8K (200 questions, greedy) through `sglang.Engine` with the arguments of `TestDSV4FlashFP4TboH200` (TP 8, attention DP 2, so attention TP 4; `--moe-a2a-backend none --moe-runner-backend marlin`, `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1`): **0.970 with TBO, 0.970 without TBO** (0.965 at the previous head).
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`'s config reduced to 4 layers and 8 experts, dummy weights, triton MoE; each TBO run compared with the same build's non-TBO run (7 requests, 8 new tokens, prompt and output logprobs): **identical** at TP 4 / attention DP 2 (attention TP 2) with eager decode, with decode CUDA graphs, and with `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1` with and without `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=1`; identical at TP 2 / attention DP 2. At the previous head the eager-decode case failed at the first decode step.
- Single short requests (TP 2 and TP 4, attention DP 2, TBO): 6/6 served; `main` crashes on the first.

### MI355X

8×MI355X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261025`, the reduced config with 256 experts and FP8 weights and the AMD TBO test's environment, TP 8 / attention DP 2:
- previous head: TBO fails ("invalid configuration argument"), the same requests without TBO pass;
- `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AG=0`: TBO passes 6/6.
- With the device-group all-gather, AMD CI at `10313c2757` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40296194792/job/121526401095)): the AMD TBO test's GSM8K (`sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8`, TP 8 / attention DP 2, so attention TP 4; 1319 questions) scored **0.955** (threshold 0.91); the non-TBO DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP4 and FP8 tests in the same job scored 0.957 and 0.951. The chat probe failed on its token budget (fixed above); the fixed probe has not run yet.

<details>
<summary>H100 validation reported before the review (TP16 / DP2 / attention TP 8)</summary>

### H100 end-to-end setup

- Model: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4`
- Hardware: 2 hosts × 8 NVIDIA H100 80GB
- Container: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260801-e4c4faf8`
- Topology: TP16 / DP2 / attention-TP8
- MoE A2A backend: `none`
- TBO enabled
- Infrastructure: [NemoRL Sandbox Infrastructure Report](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sT9QbbzXC110IC4f6T964OgKCnUouaSLYKznNnw35O8/edit?tab=t.0)

On host 0:

```bash
export NODE_RANK=0
export HEAD_NODE='<host-0 hostname>'
```

On host 1:

```bash
export NODE_RANK=1
export HEAD_NODE='<host-0 hostname>'
```

### Before: failure reproduction

The failure was reproduced both on pristine upstream `574ead753` and on the
parent of this change, `68d70aa8f`. Both reached the real two-chunk TBO path
and returned HTTP 200 responses with corrupted generated text.

The following server command was run on both hosts:

```bash

  --dist-init-addr "$HEAD_NODE:5000" \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --fp4-gemm-backend marlin \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.94 \
  --context-length 2200 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 \
  --max-running-requests 256 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000
```

This exact probe and assertion were run after the server became ready:

```bash
curl --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 180 -sS \
  "http://$HEAD_NODE:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 7 + 5? Answer with just the number."}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":32}' \
  > single.json
jq -r '.choices[0].message.content' single.json | tee single.txt
grep -q 12 single.txt
```

Pristine upstream produced:

```text

```

`grep` exited 1: **FAIL**.

The parent of this change produced:

```text
رشف3223232323232323232323a3a3a3a
```

`grep` exited 1: **FAIL**.

The parent run was Slurm job `5616864` and also recorded 48 rank-level
`is_enable_two_chunk=True` events.

The pristine-upstream run recorded 48 rank-level
`is_enable_two_chunk=True` events, representing three global two-chunk
forwards. Slurm job `5618929` completed `0:0`; completion means the harness
successfully captured the expected failure.

### After: patched result

Source `6c9e7a54a` was run with the same model, container, hosts, and topology.
The following server command was run on both hosts:

```bash

unset SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE

export SGLANG_TBO_DEBUG=1

  --enable-prefill-delayer \
  --enable-two-batch-overlap \

  --dist-init-addr "$HEAD_NODE:5000" \

  --context-length 2200 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 \
  --max-running-requests 256 \

```

This exact probe and assertion were then run:

```bash

  "http://$HEAD_NODE:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 7 + 5? Answer with just the number."}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":32}' \
  > single.json
jq -r '.choices[0].message.content' single.json | tee single.txt
grep -q 12 single.txt
```

Patched output:

```text

```

`grep` exited 0: **PASS**.

The following multi-answer check was run twice so both DP routes served it:

```bash
curl --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 180 -sS \
  "http://$HEAD_NODE:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Answer each item concisely. 1. What is the capital of France? 2. What is the capital of Japan? 3. What is 4 times 5 plus 2?"}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":192}' \

grep -qi Tokyo facts.txt &&
```

```text

2. Tokyo
3. 22
```

All three assertions exited 0: **PASS**.

The sky/seasons check also passed on both DP routes: its assertions found
`blue`, `scatter`, `season`, and `tilt`.


- 9,864 `is_enable_two_chunk=True` rank records
- Maximum logged SWA token usage: 0.80
- Request errors: 0
- Retractions: 0
- Workload CUDA/OOM/server errors: 0
- Slurm job `5616859`: `COMPLETED 0:0`

Focused collective-size tests passed 3/3 in the matching container (Slurm job
`5618770`, `COMPLETED 0:0`).

#### Speed

The 1,319-request GSM8K API phase completed in 9m01s at concurrency 16
(2.44 completed requests/s). The complete job, including checkpoint staging,
weight loading, JIT compilation, CUDA-graph capture, deterministic checks, and
GSM8K, completed in 26m03s.

The control configurations produce invalid output, so their generated-token
throughput is not a correctness-preserving performance baseline.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured after the review. The added changes only skip work on empty micro-batches, pad decode children, and change the collective that carries the attention-TP combine all-gather on ROCm.

## Verification

- CPU unit tests (`test/registered/unit/layer_boundary/`, `models/`, `model_executor/`, `batch_overlap/`, `layers/test_dp_attention*.py`): 1406 passed, 67 skipped; one failure, `test_graph_pool_borrow.py::test_graph_replay_fails_during_active_pool_borrow`, also fails at the previous head.
- The previous CI run (2026-10-21, at `1cabe14779`), failure by failure: the AMD TBO test and `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py` are addressed above; `test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py` and `test_dsv41_bcg_hip.py` were fixed on `main` after this branch's base (#45507, #45728), now merged in; the MI35x disaggregation job (UCX/RDMA setup, out of memory) and the NPU job (host out of memory in `test_npu_expert_distribution_recorder_mode.py`) do not touch this change; the gate and finish jobs follow them. `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py` runs only on four gfx950 GPUs and was not run outside CI.
- CI at `10313c2757` (2026-10-26), failure by failure: `test_hicache_l3_object_layout.py` (CPU) fails on `main` too, fixed in #46570; `test/registered/cpu/test_topk.py` (Arm64, Xeon) fails on `main` too; on Xeon, the CPU server for `test_matched_stop.py` was killed during startup (exit code -9); the AMD DeepSeek-V4 job is the chat probe above; the gate and finish jobs follow them. CUDA stages b and c did not run because stage a failed, and the remaining AMD jobs were cancelled by the push of `3a5ae846d9`.
- New tests: a micro-batch empty on every rank runs no experts; a TBO decode child pads its requests with its tokens (an extend child keeps them); the TBO shared-expert locality follows `SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL`.
